LOUISIANA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
                      GENERAL ORDER NUMBER 11-19-2026 (R-38096)

                 LOUISIANA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION, EX PARTE.

Docket No. R-38096, In re: Possible amendments to Commission General Order dated
December 20, 2024 and Special Order 46-2005 (Corrected) solely to consider increasing the cap
on the current fuel surcharge schedules for nonconsensual towing companies and motor
carriers.

                 (Decided at the October 22, 2026 Business and Executive Session.)


                                             ORDER

Overview

        Pursuant to the Notice of Proceeding and Proposed Recommendation filed on September

23, 2026, the Louisiana Public Service Commission (“LPSC” or “Commission”) opened a

rulemaking to propose amendments to Attachment A of the Schedule of Prescribed Rates and

Requirements for Non-Consensual Towing and Recovery as approved in General Order dated

December 20, 2024, as well as amending Special Order 46-2005 (Corrected) solely pertaining to

the Fuel Surcharge as set in those orders.

        Notice of this rulemaking was published in the Commission’s Official Bulletin # 1385

dated September 25, 2026 seeking comments on the proposed rules, including specific redline

proposals no later than October 15, 2026 in order to prepare Final Rules for consideration at the

Commission’s October 2026 Business and Executive Session. No interventions, nor comments

were received.

        As a part of this rulemaking, LPSC Staff proposed amendments to General Order dated

December 20, 2024 and Special Order 46-2005 (Corrected) to address the rising cost of fuel prices

and the current Fuel Surcharge index currently capped at 16% when the price of diesel fuel is $5.00

and greater. Commission Staff reviewed not only the Commission’s Orders related to the cost of

fuel, but also the U.S. Energy Information Administration’s report regarding the current retail price

of on-highway diesel fuel for the Gulf Coast region. Staff confirmed an industry concern, that the

retail price of fuel is increasing.



Applicable Law

        The Commission’s jurisdiction over common carriers and public utilities is established by

Article 4, Section 21 of the Louisiana Constitution of 1974, which provides in pertinent part:


                                                        General Order Number 11-19-2026 (R-38096)
                                                                                             Page 1
                The commission shall regulate all common carriers and public
               utilities and have such other regulatory authority as provided by law.
               It shall adopt and enforce reasonable rules, regulations, and
               procedures necessary for the discharge of its duties, and shall have
               other powers and perform other duties as provided by law.

La. R.S. 45:163 provides in pertinent part:

               A. The [public service] commission has the power and authority
               necessary to supervise, govern, regulate and control common motor
               carriers, other than a contract carrier by bus, which transport
               household goods, passengers, or waste and to fix reasonable and just
               rates, fares, tolls, or charges for the commodities furnished or
               services rendered by such motor carriers. The commission shall
               prescribe rules and regulations governing the operation of contract
               carriers in competition with common carriers, and prescribe
               minimum rates, fares and charges to be collected by such carriers.

               B. The power, authority, and duties of the commission shall include
               all matters connected with the service to be given or rendered, the
               records to be kept by motor carriers, and except as otherwise
               provided, the power to adopt and enforce such reasonable rules,
               regulations, and modes of procedure as it may deem proper for the
               discharge of its duties, to summon and compel the attendance of
               witnesses, to swear witnesses, to compel the production of books
               and papers, to take testimony under commission and punish for
               contempt as fully as is provided for by law by the district courts,
               and to prescribe and require the furnishing and filing of tariffs and
               schedules.

Pursuant to La R.S. 45:180.1,

               C. (1) The [public service] commission has power and authority
               necessary to supervise, govern, regulate, and control the business of
               the operation and use of wreckers and towing services, to designate
               classes and categories of said vehicles, to fix reasonable and just
               rates, fares, tolls, charges for storage services, or charges for the
               commodities furnished or services rendered by persons engaging in
               the operation and use of said vehicles.


Background of current Commission Orders

       A set fuel surcharge was established for non-consensual towing and recovery companies

in General Order July 5, 2000 as amended. At the February 19, 2003 Business and Executive

Session, after petition from the TRPL and in light of the volatility in fuel prices and the uncertainty

of how high the prices may ultimately go, the Commission approved a four (4) tier fuel surcharge

that was capped at 6% when the price of fuel was $2.50 and greater as memorialized in General

Order dated March 25, 2003. At the October 15, 2005 Business and Executive Session, the

Commission amended the fuel surcharge yet again on a temporary basis in light of the high fuel

cost to a sixteen (16) tier fuel surcharge that was capped at 16% when the price of fuel was $5.00

and greater and further applied the fuel surcharge to all intrastate jurisdictional transportation

companies with additional conditions as it pertained to motor carriers. The vote was memorialized

                                                         General Order Number 11-19-2026 (R-38096)
                                                                                               Page 2
 in Special Order 46-2005 (Corrected). On July 14, 2007 the TRPL requested to revise the fuel

surcharge from a sixteen (16) tier to a four (4) tier but kept the cap at 16% when the price of fuel

was $5.00 and greater, citing that the sixteen (16) tier bracket was confusing in nature. The

Commission considered the matter at the September 12, 2007 Business and Executive Session and

voted to: 1) reduce the sixteen (16) tier bracket to a six (6) tier bracket keeping the cap at 16%

when the price of fuel was $5.00 and greater; 2) no change in the top portion of the brackets if the

fuel were ever return to the $1.14 level and below a surcharge shall not be charged; 3) the basis of

the surcharge shall remain the Gulf Coast Regional and not the National average and 4) the

amendment to Special Order 46, 2005 shall be applicable only to towing and recovery professional

performing non-consensual towing. The vote was memorialized in Commission Order T-30255

dated October 3, 2007.


Staff’s Final Recommendation

       On October 16, 2026, LPSC Staff issued Notice of Staff Proposed Rules and Final

Recommendation (“Final Recommendation”). As a part of this Final Recommendation, Staff gave

notice that these proposed rules would be voted on at the LPSC October 22, 2026 Business and

Executive Session. As there was no comment on Staff’s Final Recommendation, Staff

recommended that the Commission amend Attachment A Section II of the Schedule of Prescribed

Rates and Requirements for Non-Consensual Towing and Recovery as approved in General Order

dated December 20, 2024 to read as follows:

  D. FUEL SURCHARGE

    A Tow Company shall apply the fuel surcharge on the sum of the towing, recovery, transit
    time, and extra truck and trailer charges only.
    Fuel Price (per gallon)                Fuel Surcharge
    $0.00 to $1.24                         No surcharge
    $1.25 to $1.99                         3% surcharge
    $2.00 to $2.99                         9% surcharge
    $3.00 to $3.99                         12% surcharge
    $4.00 to $4.99                         14% surcharge
    $5.00 to $5.99                         16% surcharge
    $6.00 to $6.99                         18% surcharge
    $7.00 to $7.99                         20% surcharge
    $8.00 to $8.99                         22% surcharge
    $9.00 to $9.99                         24% surcharge
    $10.00 and greater                     26% surcharge
   There shall be no change in the top portion of the brackets. If fuel ever returns to the $1.24
   level and below, a surcharge shall not be charged. The surcharge will be based on the average
   price of U.S. On-Highway Diesel Fuel as determined based upon the price reported by the
   Energy Information Administration (‘eia”) for the Petroleum Administration for Gulf
   Coast (PADD3).


                                                        General Order Number 11-19-2026 (R-38096)
                                                                                            Page 3
         Also, Staff recommended that a Commission Order in this docket supersede Special Order

46-2005 (Corrected) and adopt Attachment A to this recommendation to reflect changes to the

fuel surcharge table to read:


    Fuel Price (per gallon)        Fuel Surcharge
    Up to $.90                     3% Reduction

    $2.00 to $2.24                 4% surcharge

    $2.50 to $2.74                 6% surcharge
    $2.75 to $2.99                 7% surcharge
    $3.00 to $3.24                 8% surcharge
    $3.25 to $3.49                 9% surcharge
    $3.50 to $3.74                 10% surcharge
    $3.75 to $3.99                 11% surcharge
    $4.00 to $4.24                 12% surcharge
    $4.25 to $4.49                 13% surcharge
    $4.50 to $4.74                 14% surcharge
    $4.75 to $4.99                 15% surcharge
    $5.00 to $5.99                 16% surcharge
    $6.00 to $6.99                 18% surcharge
    $7.00 to $7.99                 20% surcharge
    $8.00 to $8.99                 22% surcharge
    $9.00 to $9.99                 24% surcharge
    $10.00 and greater             26% surcharge

Staff further recommended that:

        1. Any motor carrier, other than a non-consensual tow company, that has adopted the fuel

        surcharge contained in Special Order 46-2005 (Corrected) will be authorized to continue

        to utilized the fuel surcharge table as outlined in Attachment A to this recommendation

        and;

        2. Any motor carrier, other than a non-consensual tow company, that has its own fuel

        surcharge in its current tariff on file with the Commission, may choose to adopt the

        amended fuel surcharge table in Attachment A to any order issued in this matter, provided

        that the carrier notify the Commission in writing within 30 days of any order issued in this

        matter.

        3. The Uniform Fuel Surcharge adopted in Attachment A will no longer be considered

        temporary and will be considered a permanent fuel surcharge approved by the Commission

        until changed by the Commission.



                                                        General Order Number 11-19-2026 (R-38096)
                                                                                            Page 4
 Commission Consideration

       This matter was considered at the October 22, 2026 Business and executive Session. After

discussion, on motion of Chairman Skrmetta, seconded by Commissioner Lewis, and unanimously

adopted, the Commission voted to adopt Staff’s Proposed Recommendation filed into the record

on October 16, 2026.



IT IS THEREFORE ORDERED THAT:

   1. Attachment A Section II of the Schedule of Prescribed Rates and Requirements for Non-

      to read:

      by the Energy Information Administration (‘eia”) for the Petroleum Administration for

   2. The Special Order 46-2005 (Corrected) is superseded and Attachment A to this Order is
